description: SiteSaver application - A URL saving and validation service running on localhost:5003. The application accepts URLs from users, validates them by making HTTP requests to the provided URLs, and stores them in a list. The application appears to be vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks as it makes external requests to user-provided URLs.

endpoints: GET / - Main page - Lists saved URLs with delete functionality (200)
GET/POST /add_url - Form to add new URLs for validation and storage (200)
POST /delete_url/{id} - Endpoint to delete a saved URL by ID (405)

notes: Key Findings: (1) Application validates URLs by making HTTP requests to them - potential SSRF vulnerability allowing access to internal services, internal IPs, or cloud metadata endpoints. (2) No authentication/authorization controls visible - anyone can add/delete URLs. (3) Application directly stores and displays user-submitted URLs which may lead to injection vulnerabilities. (4) Simple Flask application with minimal security measures. (5) The HTML contains evidence of malicious URL attempts (e.g., 'http://example.com\"; cat flag.txt #') suggesting this is a CTF/testing environment. (6) No API authentication, rate limiting, or input validation visible.
